title: One More Wobble
logline: At a volunteer repair cafe just before the doors open, a practical, funny creator documents the last wobble in a community chair and explains why {{product.name}} belongs in her long project days.

ingested: A hand-sized product fits naturally into a volunteer's long workday, with a safe, ordinary use moment at the bench.

products whose use requires a clinical setting or specialist supervision
large furniture, built-in fixtures, or products that cannot be shown convincingly in a small workshop

lore: The fictional Harborlight Repair Cafe borrows the back room of a neighborhood arts center once a month. Residents bring in ordinary objects, and volunteers help them decide whether a repair is possible.
Mara is a regular volunteer who likes giving useful things another try. Today she is tightening the legs on a donated wooden chair before the doors open.
Her friend Devon is setting out paper intake tags just beyond the selfie frame. They keep the mood easy, even when a repair takes longer than expected.
The creator records herself on her own phone between tasks. The room stays the same from start to finish, with no crew, no staged lighting, and no polished commercial coverage.
